newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's 1996 tax revenue at record $22 bln.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's 1996 tax revenue at record $22 bln.

text.p: Singapore's tax revenue more than doubled in six years to a record of nearly Singapore $22 billion in 1996, the Straits Times newspaper reported Ministry of Finance figures as showing.
As a result of average growth of 8.4 percent in the 1990's, the money flowing into government coffers rose steadily to a record $21.92 billion last year, the paper reported on Saturday.

"Higher incomes as a result of high economic growth in the 1990s and the gradually expanding workforce -- which grew from 1.55 million in 1990 to about 1.75 million last year -- resulted in more income tax paid into the treasury," the paper reported.
The paper said taxes on motor vehicles amounted to $2.44 billion last year, up from 1.34 billion in 1990.

Stamp duties netted $1.83 billion, nearly three times the $655 million in 1990 due to a May regulation that required buyers to pay stamp duty up front on the value of all property sales and sub-sales.
Sellers are also required to pay stamp duty on residential properties sold within three years of purchase, it added.

Goods and services tax (GST) netted $1.79 billion last year. However this was offset by the $1.8 billion given by the state in GST rebates, it said. Tax revenue in 1990 registered $10.534 billion and in 1995 at $21.919 million.
